title: India and EU conclude talks for India to join the EU's €93.5 billion Horizon Europe research programme
dek: Indian universities, labs and companies would be able to win EU research grants directly and lead projects from January 2027, once the deal is signed and ratified. India's contribution has not been disclosed.
body:
India and the European Union have concluded negotiations for India to become an associated country of Horizon Europe, the EU's €93.5 billion research and innovation programme for 2021-27, the European Commission announced. Once the agreement is signed and ratified by both sides, association is expected to take effect in January 2027.

Association is the closest form of research cooperation the EU offers countries outside the bloc. It would allow Indian researchers, universities, research organisations and companies to receive Horizon Europe funding directly, on the same terms as those in EU member states, in return for what the Commission called a "fair financial contribution" from India to the programme's budget. The size of that contribution has not been made public.

## What changes for Indian researchers

Under association, Indian institutions would be eligible for grants paid directly by the Commission and could lead collaborative projects under the programme's second pillar, "Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness". That pillar funds work on health, digital technology, industry, space, climate, energy and the bioeconomy, according to reports.

Money will not flow automatically. Indian applicants will still have to compete in open calls and meet each call's rules on eligibility and selection, according to reports.

"The agreement opens new opportunities for our businesses," said Ekaterina Zaharieva, the EU's Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation, according to reports. "We want Europe and India to be partners in developing the technologies that will shape our future." No statement from the Indian government had been published by Saturday night.

## Background

The two sides opened exploratory talks on 6 February 2026 and began formal negotiations on 17 July, according to reports. The move builds on an India-EU science and technology cooperation agreement first signed in 2001 and since renewed to 2030, and on the joint strategic agenda to 2030 adopted at the India-EU summit on 27 January this year. Research and technology cooperation is also on the agenda of the India-EU Trade and Technology Council, which covers artificial intelligence, semiconductors, high-performance computing and 6G.

Horizon Europe now has 23 associated countries outside the EU, including the United Kingdom, Canada, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland, according to the Commission. It recently concluded similar talks with Australia.

## Why it matters

For India, association offers direct access to one of the world's largest pools of competitive research funding and closer links with European laboratories, at a time when it is trying to raise research spending and attract international collaboration. For the EU, India adds a large scientific workforce and a growing technology market. The key details, including what India will pay, will become clearer when the agreement is published for signature.

## What happens next

Both sides must now complete their legal checks, sign the agreement and ratify it under their own procedures. The Commission expects association to take effect in January 2027. Until then, Indian participants remain under the current rules, which generally do not give them EU funding of their own; afterwards, they can compete for grants in the calls that remain open.

Horizon Europe itself runs only to the end of 2027, so association would initially cover the programme's final year. What follows that depends on the EU's next research programme, on which the Commission's announcement said nothing.
